weapon_rows.quote: pistol = dagger, shotgun = the hand handgonne, car = the big one, rifle = crossbow, pipe = mace, sledge = hammer, car door = shield, bottles = throw
weapon_rows.why: each job takes the plainest row of its Battle Brothers class (a renamed thing keeps its number, rule 63d): a pipe is a bludgeon, a sledge the two-handed mallet, the rifle the light crossbow, bottles the throwing axes

crew.quote: 12 on the field in a normal fight, the roster 20
crew.why: twelve hires, each a Battle Brothers background (stats rolled in its wiki range) carrying our jobs (rule 63's weapon list) in low-tier wiki armour; the names are drafts. GUNS FIRST (rule 120(a), Paolo 10/18: 'I wanna start off with the guns too... the guns were supposed to be the main way this is gonna be solved'): the kit runs guns first in the company's order, so every company the origin builds holds a pistol and a rifle from its first two men (three men: a pistol, a rifle, a pistol; four: and a rifle; six: four guns, a sledge and a pipe); past the first four the kit builds Battle Brothers' own shape, a shieldwall in front of the guns (twelve: two pistols, three rifles, a shotgun and bottles behind two sledges and three pipes with car doors; measured 10/19: nine shooters behind three melee men could not be screened, 10 in 100 of the shooters' turns ended past the front man and 21 in 100 of the fighting turns alone, against 2 and 15 with this kit); who carries which is guns_first_kit's (the best eye takes the long gun)

guns_first.quote: every origin's first fight has guns in the company's hands, and the gun is the main way a fight is won (rule 83 stands: guns two tiles and more, melee one); the starting kit, the first band and the tutorial fight are built around shooting

first_band.quote: In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of [[Brigand Thug|Thugs]] and sometimes [[Brigand Raider|Raiders]]. Later, Raiders become more common, ranged attackers appear
first_band.why: the FIRST fight is an early one, so it is the wiki's early band: thugs and one raider, no shooters yet (they 'appear later'); twelve of ours (rule 63b) against nine. Measured: twelve against twelve with two marksmen lost 4 fights in 4. TUNING sets the real count per contract.

night.why: the first fight is by day; the loop sets night from its clock

cover_tile_blocks_line.why: a dead car or a block wall on a house tile is Battle Brothers' obstacle in the line of fire: a shot at the man behind it takes the blocked penalty; 10/4 SUPERSEDED by cover_defence (his sixth votes: cover on a man's own tile is defence by count); a car BETWEEN shooter and target still blocks the line by the wiki's 75%

perk_builds.quote: With each new character level reached by your mercenary he will gain 1 Perk point... To unlock the second perk row, you need to spend one perk point.
perk_builds.why: a hire's level is rolled in his background's starting range and each level past the first is a perk, picked in this order where its row is unlocked; the orders are the plain ones per job (a front man gets tougher, a shooter steadier); TUNING and Paolo may change them; round two puts the seven skills a perk unlocks into the orders where a job would take them (the captain's ON ME, the sledge's COME AT ME and CATCH YOUR BREATH, the pistol's FIRST OUT THE DOOR and SWAP OUT, SIDESTEP for the quick ones) (10/19, rule 120: the pistol shoots now, and its mastery stays PISTOL WORK, Battle Brothers' dagger mastery: the shot at the stab's 3 AP, three shots a turn)

board_mix.quote: Most of it won't be Nature though you know most of it will be city based terrain
board_mix.why: the board is dealt from COMBAT TWO's 21 blocks (rule 57: 'there's gonna be different map types'; sweep L: 'the board kinds must mix'): two or three kinds of one family per board, no block beside its twin, city three times in four; a named board or kind from the loop overrides; TUNING may move the weights; 10/2 round three: COMBAT TWO's round eleven renamed the suburb blocks 'subs' and added the corner, the west corner and the empty lots, so the city family carries them, and a loop asking for 'suburb' is led by one of the suburb's blocks (aliases); 10/4: COMBAT TWO's round fourteen adds MAIN STREET and THE WORKS to the city

start_cols.quote: fights start LEFT TO RIGHT on the glass, never south to north
start_cols.why: your line on column 7 facing right, theirs on column 12 facing left: five tiles between the fronts, the wiki's 'at least 5 hexes between parties' (deployment.min_gap_between_lines_hexes); back ranks one column behind each

cover_defence.quote: cars on a tile raise its defence by count (one car some, three cars more)
cover_defence.why: a man on a tile with dead cars, walls or a shed behind him gains defence per piece, up to three: three pieces are a wooden shield's +15 against swings (armor.json wooden_shield) and twice that against shots, because cars stop bullets better than they stop a pipe; TUNING owns the numbers

people_looks.quote: I wanna see all my character art that we've worked so hard on doing good work live in the game please even if it's new combat
people_looks.why: every fighter wears a look from the character bank (slices/fight_people, baked from the alpha's rig): YOU as the player stands, your eleven as the twelve city cast looks, the road crew in the runway thirteen's street factions (thugs in the poorer crews, the raider in the Mob or the Cartel); a draft pairing, his to change (10/5, [the enemy math]: the tiers wear their own crews: the raider the Mob or the Cartel, the armoured marauder the Remnants or the Blues, the shooters the Network or the Colorful, the poacher the Volunteers or the Caravans, the one leader the Church; draft)

formation_depth_lines.quote: A typical battle starts with both parties in a line formation (1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy)
formation_depth_lines.why: rule 70b: AUTO holds the formation; a man walking up may lead the middle of his line by at most the line's depth less one, so the line moves as a line; TUNING owns the number

night_lights.source: slices/fight_ground/fight_ground.json lights_key (COMBAT TWO 10/2, round twelve) and bb_all/1423_Nighttime (Status Effect).txt
night_lights.quote: a street lamp; live ones light a pool radius_m around their base (night: a lit tile plays as day)
night_lights.why: Battle Brothers' night is one status on everybody (-2 vision, -30% ranged skill, -30% ranged defence); our streets have lamps and burning drums, so the night is per tile: a man standing in a pool is seen at day range; a shooter takes the night's -30% only when his target stands in the dark; a target takes the night's -30% defence only when the shot comes out of the dark. Both lit is day, both dark is Battle Brothers' night exactly. The lesson: stay out of the light. No new number: the pool radius is COMBAT TWO's, the penalties the wiki's.

formation.quote: In the lower right corner of the inventory screen you now have three rows with 9 slots each. The lower row is your reserves; characters placed here do not take part in battle. The top two rows are your front and back battle lines, allowing you to place archers in the back and build a sturdy shieldwall in front.
formation.why: COMBAT [your formation] (Paolo's sixth votes: 'formation and gear are the depth'; GROK_75: 'the front line and the back line are already set by how you layered the company before the fight'). The fight opens with your men where the roster's two rows put them: slot 1 to 9 of the front row stand top to bottom on your front column, the back row one column behind. The roster order is RUN TWO's (FIGHT_OPTS.formation {front:[...], back:[...]}, crew indices or null); until its roster screen exists the default is Battle Brothers' own advice: the shieldwall in front, the shooters behind, in roster order, centred. Before turn one you may move any man to any tile of your two columns (ours: Battle Brothers sets this on the company screen; our roster screen is not built, so the fight hosts it); END TURN reads FIGHT and starts it; AUTO skips it.

enemy_tiers.source: bb_all/0299_Brigands.txt (the tactics), bb_all/0290_Brigand Leader.txt, bb_all/0293_Brigand Marauder.txt, bb_all/0297_Brigand Raider.txt, bb_all/0294_Brigand Marksman.txt (Bullseye after day 20); reference/library/grok/GROK_60_ENEMY_MATH_2026_10_02.md
enemy_tiers.quote: In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of Thugs and sometimes Raiders. Later, Raiders become more common, ranged attackers appear and their numbers increase, and armored Marauders can spawn. In the late game you will usually see a Brigand Leader and other elite enemies among them. / Brigand Leaders start appearing in the middle game. Late game brigand groups usually have a Leader. It's rare to see simultaneously more than one. / Melee skill is 65 before day 40, 70 after. / (GROK_60) Combat difficulty, set at the start, raises both the count and the tier. Higher tier means more leaders and fewer thugs. Day scaling for those stops at day 100. A few is 2 to 3. Some is 4 to 6. / (Brigand Marksman) Ranged defense is 10 before day 40, 15 after.
enemy_tiers.why: COMBAT [the enemy math] (Paolo 10/5, rule 75b: 'the beginning is a lot different from the end'). The map hands the party (RUN [a few, not twelve]: the count, the days, the difficulty); the fight dresses it by tier. The phase boundaries are the wiki's own day gates (perks after day 20, the raider's skill after day 40, the marauder's best armour after day 60) and Grok's day 100 where roaming scaling stops; each combat difficulty above Veteran moves the tier as if the party were 20 days later (Beginner and Veteran the same); a party of 'some' (4) or more in the late phase brings its one leader. The mix weights are ours from the tactics paragraph; TUNING owns every one. A skill or a defence the wiki gives as a range (65-70, 10-15) is the before-and-after of skill_day, never a roll. THE BEASTS (COMBAT [the fight holds the grid], rule 117(e), 10/18): the pack's make-up is FACTIONS' draft for the lab-made beasts (records/target/bb/factions.json, faction beasts: early four dire wolves to two hyenas, late three dire wolves, two frenzied, one schrat); the middle phase keeps the early pack until a source says when the frenzied ones join; TUNING owns every weight.

first_week.quote: the starting kit, the first band and the tutorial fight are built around shooting / In the early game Brigand groups usually consist of Thugs and sometimes Raiders
first_week.why: THE FIRST BAND IS BUILT TO BE SHOT AT: the company's first week (days 1 to 7) meets thugs alone, the wiki's early band before its 'sometimes Raiders'; the lesser raider (75 health, 55 to 110 body armour) joins from day 8. Measured 10/19 before it: a fresh crew of three met two raiders in one band of three and lost every time, whatever it carried. The beasts' first week is their early pack. TUNING owns the day.

captain_aura.quote: Captain is an aura that increases the Resolve of other allies by +15% (range of 5 tiles)
captain_aura.why: the brigand leader carries it (enemies.json: perks and skills 'Captain'); his men within five tiles check their nerve at 115% resolve

board_fit.quote: the actual combat map doesn't need to be so big in Battle Brothers unless it's an endgame battle or three raiding parties hit you at the same time, 12 versus 60... on the map I want to see it more zoomed in / (the wiki) A typical battle starts with both parties in a line formation (1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy), with at least 5 hexes between parties.
board_fit.why: COMBAT [the board fits the party]: the board is cut from the dealt board to the parties: across, a tile of room behind each line, the two lines' depths and the wiki's five-tile gap between their fronts; down, the longer line and a tile of room above and below. The full board only for the endgame (FIGHT_OPTS.endgame) or when the handover carries three parties or more (party.parties). TUNING owns the margin.

struck_down_injury.source: bb_all/1540_Permanent Injuries.txt and VAMILY.md 04 COMBAT [struck down] (Paolo's fifth votes)
struck_down_injury.quote: Permanent injuries are incurable disabilities received after having been struck down in battle... The part hit does not matter in selecting the injury. / (Paolo) a veteran struck down dies 20 percent of the time, else a long injury from injuries.json
struck_down_injury.why: a man struck down who lives carries one of the wiki's permanent injuries (all equally likely, the body part not mattering, as the wiki says), and ours lasts the days he is laid up (ours.struck_down_laid_up_days), Paolo's 'debilitating injury 30 to 40 days'; the roster reads it as one pain line

built_piece.quote: building: a piece that blocks, drawn with its own picture
built_piece.why: the footprint in metres of a building you put up at a place, as it stands on the fight's board (LIFE+CITY's numbers, moved here by COMBAT 10/10 so the fight's rules type no number, rule 63d); its own picture is ../settlement/lot/<id>.png

gun_classes.source: records/BOHEMIA_PAOLO_ZONE_OF_CONTROL_IS_MELEE_ONLY_10_10_26.md (rule 103) and records/target/bb/weapon_lines.json (our skins: dagger = PISTOL, firearm = SHOTGUN, crossbow = RIFLE)
gun_classes.quote: if any person does not have a melee weapon currently equipped, they don't get a zone of control; zone of control is only for melee, one tile next to them; anyone using a ranged weapon has no zone of control and you can just walk left, up, right, down, across their tiles
gun_classes.why: Battle Brothers' dagger carries our PISTOL, so by Battle Brothers' rule it still held a zone of control; a gun in his hands is a gun whatever its row underneath, and holds none (bows and bottles are already ranged)

gun_min_range.quote: melee weapons work on one tile away, all guns 2+ minimum
gun_min_range.why: a gun that fires (ours.gun_classes that are ranged: the SHOTGUN, the RIFLE, and from 10/19 the PISTOL's shot, ours.pistol_shot) never fires at a man beside the shooter; the pistol is the club at one (rule 83: 'the pistol is a two-tile gun, or a club at one'); its shot came with rule 120, the guns vote rule 47b waited for

ground_rows.quote: every floor tile from Battle Brothers needs a proper translation for our game... how it impacts your accuracy or your defence or the positioning, how many action points it costs to move through
ground_rows.rows_from: records/target/BOHEMIA_GROUND_EFFECTS.json battleBrothersRows (WORLD's one table; rule 59: never a second list of grounds)
ground_rows.why: every tile kind COMBAT TWO's 35 blocks draw answers to ONE row of WORLD's ground table: flat is Battle Brothers' plains (2 AP, nothing else), rough and rubble its forest floor and snow (3 AP), water its swamp (4 AP, skill and defence x0.75), a roof its hills (+1 AP to climb, +10 to hit down, -10 up for melee, +1 reach a level for guns), a wall or a house its obstacles (no path, no sight). The numbers stay in records/target/bb (TUNING holds every one at Battle Brothers for both sides, rule 117). 'say' is the line he reads when he taps a tile that changes something (an attempt, draft:true); a tile that changes nothing says nothing (rule 117b: one clear next thing)

beast_looks.source: slices/fight_beasts/fight_beasts.json (ANIMATION, rules 42 and 69: the dire wolf, the one beast sheet baked) and laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_BEASTS_ARE_LAB_MADE_AND_THE_BESTIARY_FLOOR_9_29_26.md
beast_looks.quote: every beast is a de-extinct animal that broke out of its lab when the dollar died
beast_looks.why: COMBAT [the fight holds the grid] (rule 117(e)): which baked beast sheet an enemy wears on the board. The dire wolf is its own; the other four-legged hunters (the hyena, the wolf, the war dog) wear the dire wolf's sheet as a STAND-IN until ANIMATION bakes each, said on every card that shows one. An enemy not listed is drawn from the band's people looks (the schrat, the unhold and the rest have no sheet yet: a stand-in man, named in the record).

guns_first_kit.source: VAMILY.md rule 120(a); records/target/bb/backgrounds.json (each background's ranged_skill and melee_skill ranges, the wiki's)
guns_first_kit.quote: every origin's first fight has guns in the company's hands, and the gun is the main way a fight is won
guns_first_kit.why: the company's kit (the crew rows' jobs, in order) is dealt to the men the origin built before a fight that hands no gear (YOU keep the company's first slot, your own pistol and car door: measured 10/19, the best eye made the level-four captain a rifleman, whose perks are all passive, and the auto brain used no perk skill in twelve fights): the long guns first, each to the man whose background has the best eye (the middle of its wiki ranged_skill range), the melee jobs next to the best arms (melee_skill), the pistols and the bottles to the rest in the line's order. A New Crew's ranged companion takes the rifle, the one-hand and two-hand companions the pistols. Gear the roster hands over (RUN TWO) always wins.

pistol_shot.quote: melee weapons work on one tile away, all guns 2+ minimum / the pistol is a two-tile gun, or a club at one / I wanna start off with the guns too... the guns were supposed to be the main way this is gonna be solved
pistol_shot.why: our PISTOL is Battle Brothers' dagger (weapon_lines.json, the market's CLASSNAME), a one-tile row, so it never fired: rule 83's two-tile floor shut its only strike out of every shot. Rule 120 is the guns vote rule 47b waited for. A pistol now SHOOTS from two tiles as Battle Brothers' own one-handed missile, the throwing class (range 2 to 4, Throw Javelin's 4 AP and 15 fatigue, +20 to hit and -10 a tile past two, its uses as the rounds it carries), each pistol riding the javelin row of its own price rank (the knife the crude javelins, the dagger and the notched blade the javelins, the rondel, the qatal and the estoc the heavy ones); at ONE tile it is the club its own row always was (Stab, Puncture). The shot's damage, armour and rounds are the javelin row's; its weight, price and name stay the pistol's. An enemy picks a pistol last (the wiki's early bands carry no shooters). THE ROUNDS ARE A MAGAZINE (10/19, measured: with five uses for the whole fight the company fired eleven shots a fight whatever the gap, and shooting could never be the main way it is won): the ridden row's uses are the rounds in the gun, and an empty pistol reloads them all with Battle Brothers' crossbow Reload (the light crossbow's row: 4 AP, its fatigue), only when it is empty (rule 117(b): one clear next thing). The rounds the company carries between fights are ECONOMY's [the first bullets].

hit_roll_shift.source: VAMILY.md rule 117(a) (Paolo 10/18); banks/BOHEMIA_TUNING_RULE_117_EASIER_THAN_BB_10_18_26.json combat.hit_roll_shift; records/BOHEMIA_TUNING_THE_DIFFICULTY_STEPS_EXACTLY_10_9_26.md s2 (the wiki, Game Mechanics: Difficulty levels)
hit_roll_shift.quote: Beginner: your hit roll 5 points better (roll minus 5), enemy hit roll 5 points worse (roll plus 5) / I want you to be easier than Battle Brothers
hit_roll_shift.why: points on your men's hit chance and off theirs, by the door's fights pick (party_math.json difficulty_by_pick: NEW HERE 0, SEEN IT 1, OUTLIVED IT 2; 3 has no door pick): NEW HERE and SEEN IT, the door's default, play at Battle Brothers' Beginner (rule 117(a): their default sits at our hard end, the sliders go up from ours); OUTLIVED IT is their Veteran, our hard end; the fourth step past it. It is inside the number on the tile (TUNING: SHOWN inside the hit number), never hidden.

gun_club.source: VAMILY.md rule 83 (Paolo 10/10) and rule 120(a) (Paolo 10/18); records/target/bb/ours.json weapon_rows (a pipe is their mace: the bludgeon)
gun_club.quote: melee weapons work on one tile away, all guns 2+ minimum / the pistol is a two-tile gun, or a club at one / the guns were supposed to be the main way this is gonna be solved
gun_club.why: a gun never fires at a man beside the shooter (rule 83), so a gunman a thug reaches was helpless: measured 10/19, the auto brain walked him out of the thug's reach and he ate the free swing, and the guns kit lost to the pipes kit 63 to 88 in 100 on three thugs. Every gun (ours.gun_classes and the pistol's shot) is a CLUB AT ONE, his own words for the pistol: at one tile it strikes as the plainest row of Battle Brothers' club class, the bludgeon (the pipe's own row, Bash 4 AP), and a gunman with his club does not step out of a man's reach. Both sides: an enemy's crossbow is a rifle too. It holds no ring (rule 103: a gun in his hands holds none).

weapon_says_weak.quote: the game doesn't explain to you at all that your weapon sucks / before a shot or a swing, under the finger, the hit chance and what it does to that target's armour, and one plain line when the weapon is bad for it ('your pipe barely dents his plate'); after it, what it did
weapon_says_weak.why: the one plain line comes up when the arm in his hand needs this many body blows or more to drop the man he aims at, his armour wearing down blow by blow (the fight's own damage math at the weapon's middle damage, FIGHT.preview). Measured 10/19 over the company's six arms: a fresh crew drops a day-one thug in 2 to 4 blows (no line: the first fight is not a lecture), a pistol needs 5 for a lesser raider, everything but the sledge 8 to 21 for a leader or a marauder in plate. When a man of his drops that one in fewer, the line names him. TUNING owns the number.
